title: Close out Phase 1: retro + plan Phase 2
description: Retro on the Phase 1 run, fold learnings into .tick/learnings.md within the 150-line cap, verify the epic outside-in against a live cloud run, then plan the Phase 2 epic (1vn, cloud substrate fan-out) against what the single-sandbox run actually taught.
notes:
2026-08-19 21:47 - When planning Phase 2 (1vn) during this closeout, you MUST create the sandbox benchmarking tick — the human asked for it explicitly on 2026-08-19 and the full brief is recorded on 1vn (cold/warm/hot start, per-stage breakdown, fan-out at N=1/3/5, cost per run, and the three assumptions the numbers are meant to settle). Do not let it survive only as a note: it is a deliverable with an acceptance criterion, and it is the first chance to replace this epic's image-size and caching assumptions with measurements.
2026-08-20 04:36 - RETRO — epic ko8 (Phase 1: single-sandbox cloud run)

OUTSIDE-IN VERIFICATION against the epic's definition of done, item by item:
- 'branches and a PR appear on the remote' — NOT YET VERIFIED. Needs the GitHub PAT (gate kbn).
- 'gates reach Telegram and can be answered from a phone' — NOT YET VERIFIED end to end; the delivery path is built (kv2) and unit-covered.
- 'the run cost comes from AI Gateway telemetry' — built (k2s) and now enforceable: the operator's token gained gateway access and two gateways exist.
- 'tk cloud status reports it live' — VERIFIED against the deployed factory.
- 'tk cloud stop produces a clean stop' — built and unit-covered; not exercised on a live run.
- 'a killed sandbox is replaced and the run still finishes' — built (ldr); Phase 2 tick s7f makes reconcile-on-reboot correct.
- 'a second submission refuses naming the lease holder' — built (afj/daq) and unit-covered.
- Deployment itself — VERIFIED LIVE: image built from source at the deployed commit and pushed, container application ticks-orchestrator deployed, Worker + ticks-run Workflow live, /health reports sandboxes/run_rooms/artifacts/db/run_workflow all true, all four D1 migrations applied to the live database, and tk cloud run authenticates and is refused with the designed actionable gateway message.

HONEST STATUS: the epic is deployed and correct up to the credential boundary. It is NOT done, because its definition of done requires a completed end-to-end run and that needs a GitHub PAT only the operator can mint (kbn, awaiting work). Per the no-known-failure-closes rule this epic stays open rather than being relabelled.

WHAT THE PROCESS CAUGHT — the theme of this epic:
Four defects reached a green test suite and were caught only by running the real thing: PBKDF2 over Cloudflare's undocumented-locally 100k cap; an npx probe returning npm's version and hijacking wrangler resolution; kv2 breaking the offline tk ask/answer path; and — found by this very closeout — NO SANDBOXES BINDING AT ALL, so a complete, correct, deployed control plane would have refused every run. The gate, the foundation review and the final review each caught things the others could not. The lesson to carry into Phase 2: for platform-hosted code, a deploy is part of the gate, not a follow-up.

LEARNINGS PROMOTED to .tick/learnings.md (149 lines, under cap): factory test isolation (a run left un-ended times out the NEXT test file in the shared workerd runtime); the image builds tk from source at the deploying commit so it cannot predate the code it runs, which makes a branch push a prerequisite of the image build.

PHASE 2 PLANNED (1vn): 8 ticks over 4 waves — per-tick containers with the three spawn defences, substrate=cloud for local orchestrators sharing one lease, reconcile-on-reboot, run_event producers, plus the benchmarking (kuf) and declared-image (x3v) ticks. Given a goal-compatible definition of done, which this epic lacked at planning time and had to be granted retroactively.
2026-08-21 10:15 - RETRO ADDENDUM — the four P0s found by running the thing for real (2026-08-21)

Phase 1 shipped a control plane that was correct up to the credential boundary. Then one real run
of epic 72y — 892 calls, 4.4 hours, seven ticks implemented — exposed four defects that every green
suite had missed, and lost all seven ticks. Each is now closed:

- cts: the cost query trusted result_info.total_pages, a field the gateway logs API does not send.
  Defaulted to 1, stopped after 50 of 892 entries, reported $2.98 against a real $49.80 and a $25
  ceiling. A budget fed by a truncated query is not a budget.
- gyl: the kill switch was decorative — NOT because the per-request revocation check was wrong (it
  was right, and tested) but because supervisePass minted a fresh token at every boot, and closeout
  ran with enforce_budgets:false so it read no stop record at all. Only container deletion stopped
  the run. Durability is now a refusal to MINT, checked before every boot.
- tpl: nothing reached origin until closeout, so the seven implemented ticks died with the
  container. Now a keeper loop pushes tick-run/<epic> on a timer, from the container, mechanically.
- l8z: 46M input tokens at zero cache hits. Workers AI prefix caching needs x-session-affinity,
  which the gateway never set. Now stamped from the run id, with the injected prompt pinned
  byte-identical so one varying token cannot invalidate the prefix.

Plus fw6, filed from a billing audit rather than a failure: the factory could route to anthropic,
openai or openrouter, and the only thing preventing cash spend was the ABSENCE of a vendor key.
Now workers-ai is the sole default route and the refusal states the billing consequence.

THE PATTERN. Every one of these is the green-start trap in a new costume: a permissive default
(total_pages -> 1), a check that something else undoes (revoke -> re-mint), an absence mistaken for
a guarantee (no vendor key -> no cash route), and a header nobody set (no affinity -> no caching).
The suites were green because each was internally consistent. What caught them was spending real
money for four hours. Phase 2's benchmarking tick (kuf) is the deliberate version of that.

BILLING, now confirmed on the operator dashboard rather than assumed: Workers AI is credit-covered
(Startup Program caps Workers AI at $50k, R2 at $10k); AI Gateway is excluded. Cloudflare classifies
gateway-routed Workers AI as Workers AI — 4.54M Neurons on deepseek-v4-pro, matching the gateway
log's dollar figure. Mid-cycle billable usage showed none of it, which is lag, not absence. Two
follow-ups filed on 1vn: h4n (assert postpaid billing mode) and wn5 (per-run budget flags).

CEILINGS. RUN_MAX_COST_USD 25 -> 5 and RUN_MAX_WALL_CLOCK_MS 6h -> 45m, deliberately small until a
run is measured with enforcement that works. These are safety numbers, not capacity numbers; raise
them from measurement, not from a stalled run.
2026-08-21 14:21 - OUTSIDE-IN VERIFICATION CLOSED (2026-08-21). The epic's definition of done required a completed end-to-end cloud run. Run a1f87597 on the one-tick smoke epic gj9 delivered it, unassisted:

  tick gj9: repair EPIC-SKELETON (review 9f5, closeout npz)
  tick iit: report FAILED on cleanup per-tick line when apply fails
  Merge branch 'tick/gj9/iit' into tick-run/gj9
  tick iit: close after integrated gate passed
  tick 9f5: final review clean, close review
  tick npz: close-out verified, PR 50 merged, close epic gj9

PR #50 merged to main at 12:02:36. The fix is live: cmd/tk/cmd/herd_cleanup.go now
reports FAILED on the per-tick line, with a 36-line test the implementer wrote.

Numbers: 78 minutes, 154 calls, $4.47, 63.5% of input tokens cached. The run's own
progress verdict was "advanced - 2 branches on origin changed while the run was alive
(main, tick-run/gj9)".

Every item previously marked NOT YET VERIFIED is now closed by this run:
- branches and a PR appear on the remote - VERIFIED (PR 50, merged)
- the run cost comes from AI Gateway telemetry - VERIFIED (trip fired on it)
- tk cloud stop produces a clean stop - VERIFIED, both variants: --now on run
  62c289d1 (revoked 1 credential, spending stopped between call 229 and 230), and
  the wall-clock trip on a1f87597 which hard-revoked at 11:31:59 and still unwound
  into a closeout that completed the epic on a fresh credential.
- a killed sandbox is replaced and the run still finishes - VERIFIED (attempt 2)
Still unverified end to end: Telegram gates answered from a phone (kv2 is built and
unit-covered only).

WHAT THE MEASURED RUNS ADDED. Phase 1 shipped a control plane that was correct up to
the credential boundary; running it for real then produced ten defects no suite had
caught, five of them closed in this epic (cts, gyl, tpl, l8z, fw6, 4ef) and five filed
for Phase 2 (kji, uzx, fxf, vy2, l4l). The pattern is one thing wearing different
costumes: a permissive default (total_pages -> 1), a check something else undoes
(revoke -> re-mint), an absence mistaken for a guarantee (no vendor key -> no cash
route), a header nobody set (no affinity -> no caching), and a lease nobody renewed
during boot. Every suite was green because each was internally consistent.

The single most useful artifact is the cost model, now in repo-wiki/cloud-factory-billing.md:
a cached input token costs 0.004 neurons against 0.120 uncached, one thirtieth. That
ratio, not the model choice, is what decides what a run costs.
closed_reason: Completed: Phase 1 is verified outside-in by a cloud run that took a one-tick epic from plan to merged PR unassisted — worktree, implementer, test, integrated gate, final review, closeout, PR 50 to main — for $4.47 with 63.5% of its input tokens cached. Learnings are compacted to the 150-line cap and Phase 2 is planned against measurements rather than assumptions.
